newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Zaldivar mine says no damage from quake.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Zaldivar mine says no damage from quake.

text.p: Minera Zaldivar said its copper mine had suffered no damage from a quake that briefly shook a northern region of Chile earlier on Monday.
Zaldivar's risk prevention manager, Julio Poblete, told Reuters the earth had trembled for a few seconds early this morning but without any consequences for the mine.

Chile's National Office of Emergencies (ONEMI) had reported earlier that an earthquake measuring 4.8 degrees on the Richter scale had rocked the region near Zaldivar, adding that no injuries or damages were reported.
Minera Zaldivar is jointly owned by Finland's Outokumpu Oy and Canada's Placer Dome. A spokesman for the mining company was not immediately available for comment.

The tremor was also felt in Antofagasta, a coastal city 1,400 km (875 miles) north of Santiago. The epicenter was about 170 km (105 miles) east of Antofagasta, while its ipocenter was about 94 km (60 miles) below the surface, ONEMI said.
